character_book.name: AA/A/B/O/FO - Sex and Genders
character_book.description:
There are the biological sexes, male and female. Primary genders are what someone presents as, as it is in real society. Sub-genders, or secondary genders, are known as Alpha, Beta, and Omega.
Alphas and Omegas have hierarchy levels within their class which are known as Apex Alphas and Fecund Omegas. Apex, in general, means something that is peak or at the top, while fecund means fertile.
Apex Alphas: in the past, were in the position of rulers and took another Alpha, but not Apex, or omega as their mate. Apex Alphas are above other Alphas and stand at the top of the hierarchy, which is presented by their powerful and strong scents, which they can expand their scent from a single hotel room to the entire hotel floor the room is on. Able to easily overpower the strongest “average” alpha. Can “mate” successfully with all orders like the Fecund Omega. Apex Alphas make 2% of the Alpha population.
Alpha: The half population that makes up for the 23% of the population. In the Alpha order, they make up the 23% out of 25%. Can “mate” with a beta but there are more struggles compared to “mating” with a regular or Fecund Omega. They can only expand their scent in which area it can influence, example; the average expansion their scent can influence is a single hotel room.
Beta: The class that makes up the a/b/o scale, 50% are beta while the other 50% consists of Alphas and Omegas. Just your average person except for a few qualities like;
-Being able to faintly catch onto how all alphas and all omegas smell like
-They can’t growl or purr but they can chitter, they can only chitter when they are: comforting, extremely excited, very depressed or stressed, and frustrated
-While they can’t enlarge their canines the ring around their pupil can darken or lighten up in sync with positive or negative emotions
While the majority of betas follow the “Alpha remains with Omega” pair, unusual pairings are also accepted by most beta population. They have no need to mark their mate, but they can still leave their mark bond when paired with Alphas or Omegas. Beta pairs can occasionally have a Alpha or Omega offspring, while it is extremely rare for beta pairs to have an Apex or Fecund offspring it is not unheard of.
Omega: The half that makes up the 24% of the population. In the omega order, they make up the 24% out of 25%. On most occasions, omegas generally have one “pup” at a time though there are the rare few that can have “litters” their first pregnancies are usually singular. While most omegas are more sociable there have been a good bunch of omegas that prefer solitary lives, these omegas are occasionally referred to as “runts” or “stray-mega". Omega heats can usually fill up a room they are in but can leave traces if they leave the room, their heats last around four days.
Fecund Omegas: in the past, were treated akin to livestock due to their high probability of pregnancy, even higher than other Omegas. Their place was generally not recorded, used simply to produce an Alpha’s heir and other nobility would do the same. A Fecund Omega’s scent is said to be able to spurr an Alpha into a prolonged rut cycle. In the recent times they still prefer to hide being a Fecund due to human traffickers that sees them as an easy profit, as most of rich famlies would buy an Fecund for a high price. Compared to regular omegas in heat, a Fecund heat gives off a stronger smell and can reach the outdoors, they last for minimum a week. Fecund omegas tend to have a more confident persona than regular omegas and can often be confused for “runts” and “stray-megas” until their scent reaches the individual. Unlike the “average” omega, Fecund Omegas can have a litter of “pups” on their first pregnancies rarely do they have one child on their first pregnancies, a single pup from a Fecund is usually born at the 2nd or 3rd pregnancy. Can “mate” successfully with all orders like the Apex Alpha. Fecund Omegas make 1% of Omega population.
Sub-genders can vary from when they are presented. Signs can show as early as 4-6 years old, but it is not officially recorded until they experience a heat/rut, which presents itself within this time period. An official cycle, or adult cycle, is presented at the end of puberty. Scents are presented first, but can evolve as the sub-gender fully presents itself.
All omegas can go into a “feral” state, usually when it has to do with an item they hold dearly or when they feel extremely threatened (it is especially boosted when they have pups).
If an omega is in a “feral” state it is best if someone they know or feel secure with is there to calm them down since nothing else can take an omega out of that state.
Omegas bring their items most special to them to have their potential “mate” scent them, if someone else intends to court an omega they usually make something for them.
All males are born with a penis. All females are born with a vagina. This does not change. An Alpha female will still have their biologically female anatomy, but will also have a penis. Male Omegas will still have their penis, and their uterus will be attached via their anus.
Male Omegas cannot impregnate and commonly have cesarean section done. Less than 0.001% of pups are pushed out of a male Omega. This could cause damage to both parties.
Alpha females retain ovaries and can get pregnant, however, the probability of pregnancy is less than 0.01%. The penis of the Alpha is also sheathed unless aroused, and therefore about to engage in intercourse.
Despite all of this, there is a delicate process to reverse or “switch” one’s sub-gender. This is known either as “bitching” or “studding”.

entries.name: Collars
entries.content:
Sub-genders wear collars to distinguish their class. This is because some Omegas or Alphas will cover up their scent due to personal reasons. Collars are given to the Alpha/Omega after the end of their first “true” heat/rut when they are about 15-18 years of age (when puberty ends). Omegas and Alphas will present before this, but it becomes official when they experience their adult heat/rut.
Adult heats/ruts are the common idea of the cycle you’re used to seeing in fanfiction. There are other classifications of the cycles, and I’ve decided that mild heats and ruts can occur when puberty begins. Collars are still given when the adult cycle is finished, but presentation comes before that.
Presentation can begin with scents, as well as a mini heat/rut. These are much more milder than the adult cycles in which they occur when the young Alpha/Omega finds themselves craving physical attention and affection. Typically, this lasts less than a week, around 3-5 days, and is dealt with by family (or pack) cuddles. Warmth and familiar scents sate the instincts of the Alpha/Omega and these mini cycles typically occur once every 3 years until puberty begins.
Apex Alphas wear gold collars, Alphas wear black. Omegas wear white collars, while Fecund Omegas wear silver. Betas do not wear collars and it is frowned upon for a Beta to wear an accessory that can be mistaken as a collar (chokers mostly, but thicker or tighter necklaces are also “forbidden”).
Sometimes Fecunds get a white collar from their Omega family members or frends, they also use scent blockers and heat blockers.

entries.name: Scenting
entries.content:
Scents are what every individual has. Each person, Alpha, Beta, or Omega, has a unique scent. Most of the time, Alpha scents are more earthy and overwhelming. Omega scents are usually rich and sweet. Scent glands, in general, overlap with sweat glands.
Scenting is the action of rubbing one’s scent glands on their mate. This can be done for plenty of reasons, but it does feed into the protective and often possessive nature of an Alpha. Bonded mates do not have to worry about scenting as much due to their bond carrying the scent.
An Alpha’s scent comes from their neck, inner thighs/genital area, underarms, shoulders, and tips of fingers. Most Alphas scent their mates by rubbing their neck on theirs. Some will even rub the tips of the fingers along their mate’s neck. Apex Alphas are not much different, but do have a stronger intensity in the areas than if they were regular Alphas.
An Omega’s scent comes from their neck up to their ears, inner wrists, and inner thigh/genital area. Omegas can scent their mate, but the smell will not linger as strongly as an Alpha’s scent. Fecund Omegas block their scents completely due to the danger of being exposed as a Fecund.
Betas do have scents, however, they cannot smell their own scent nor smell others. They have instincts to determine if someone is another class, but that’s all. Most Beta scents are more subdued and natural, similar to an ocean or a summer day.

entries.name: Relationships
entries.content:
Typically, a mate is an Alpha’s or Omega’s partner. A Beta’s partner is usually just that, a partner/significant other/etc. This is mostly because only Alphas and Omegas can bond with someone else, therefore claiming a mate. Betas lack the instincts to claim a mate and create a bond mark.
Bonding or Marking is the intimate action of putting a mark on a mate. Bond marks should be a conscious decision on the Alpha/Omega’s accord but sometimes are not, and they break skin. A bond gives the mate an increased sense involving their mate, even if they’re far apart.
The "Mark" is put during sex in a heat cycle, when a alpha bits the omega in their neck. If he was "marked" the alpha won't change but the omega can't have any more partners. If the omega have sex with someone other then the one who marked them, they will suffers from dizziness, headache, passing out, and other symptoms, this doesn't have a solution.

entries.name: Heats
entries.content:
PRE-HEAT:
Three to five days before heat begins, Omegas will go into what is known as pre-heat. During this time, they will have the urge to start to nest. Nesting is generally making up a small, comfortable place to ride out a heat. The area will be filled with blankets, pillows, and things that remind the Omega of their Alpha (if they have one). Oftentimes, Omegas also find themselves being extremely hungry during pre-heat, as their bodies are trying to compensate for when heat itself hits and the Omega has little care for eating or drinking. Omegas may sleep more during a pre-heat to conserve the energy they will need for their heat, and often find themselves overheating mildly, especially while asleep. Pre-heat ends when the Omega goes fully into heat.
HEAT:
When pre-heat ends, the Omega goes immediately into heat. Heat lasts from 4-7 days, for Fecunds 5-14 days, and begins with fever, mild cramping, increased slick, and increased pheromone production. The increased pheromones are biology's way of luring mates, and it signals to any Alphas in the area that the Omega is fertile. Betas may also feel the pull to breed with an Omega in heat, but the draw on them is far less than it is on Alphas.
As heat really gets going, slick production ramps up even further. If they don't get knotted the cramps only worsen. The desire to mate becomes anywhere from a low-grade need that is easy to brush off to a desire that, if not relieved in some way, can become almost entirely debilitating. Unmated Omegas have many options to get relief, including asking a friend to be their heat partner (always set up before a full heat, as the Omega's judgement may be a bit skewed if they are in pain or uncomfortable), using toys (generally while masturbating), using an Alpha service, using an Alpha's scent, or any combination of the above. It is generally agreed that toys and masturbation are the least fulfilling of the options, but it can take away enough of the immediacy to allow the Omega to function. Some unmated Omegas may lock themselves into their room or nest voluntarily to stop themselves from trying to convince others to help them through heat.
There are medications that can help to extend the time between heats, or even stop them altogether. Suppressants are an option that many Omegas use. Modern suppressants are safe and generally effective, but constant use can have unwanted side effects. Some Omegas have used the wrong medication (street or non-regulated versions) and have rendered themselves infertile. Taking full suppressants for a long period leaves an Omega who comes off of them with the very real possibility of having a heat that is much more intense than they had before the suppressants. Mini-pills, as they are generally referred to, stop a full heat, but leave the Omega with small heats (also known as pseudo-heats) in their stead. Mini-pills are generally considered safe to take for up to six months at a time, with a one month break in between to allow the Omega's body a chance to have one full heat. Studies have shown that this treatment is safe and effective for up to three years, and then the pills must be changed or discontinued.
Heats tend to go in waves. Once an Omega has gotten some relief, the heat tends to "back down" for a while. This time is the perfect time to get something light and easy to eat down, and to drink as much water as possible. It's also the perfect time for naps! The cycle continues over the 4-7 days, though the last day tends to be the least intense.
POST HEAT:
An Omega in post heat will likely sleep, a lot. The use of energy in the heat was intense, and the Omega's body is doing its best to bring the Omega back to tip-top shape again. Omegas have been known to sleep for 15 hours at a time in post heat, only waking to use the restroom before going back to sleep. With a mate or a friend to help, Omegas can be woken up to eat and drink every four to six hours, and this will help them to return to themselves that much faster. Once the post heat time passes, the Omega's body continues on its cycle, and in two to three weeks, it will all start anew.

entries.name: Ruts
entries.content:
Rut is a period of time in which Alphas feel the overwhelming need to breed. Alphas generally go into rut every three months, though with a bonded Omega mate, their ruts may align with their Omega partner's heats. Ruts tend to make Alphas more aggressive toward any other Alphas who might come near their Omega/bond-mate. Most Alphas get very overprotective of Omegas they think of as in their care as the rut takes hold. They are generally much more sexually active during a rut, since the biological drive to breed is what is guiding them. They'll constantly try to mate their partner during this time until they eventually fall asleep. An Alpha can have a much easier time being alone during a rut than an Omega in heat. There are amazing sex toys on the market of every size and shape, and artificial slick to be used. As long as they orgasm and knot, it will help to bring the rut down in intensity. Of course, most Alphas would prefer the real thing, but if it's not available there is the option.
In a bonded pair, when the rut coincides with heat, it tends to make both much more intense. The hormones are essentially doubled, as they are both feeding into each other. Bond-mated Alphas may find themselves growling at anyone who comes near their home, and their protective side is amplified significantly. With a Bond-mate, Alphas have been known to go into rut at every one of their heats. This often leads to time off of work for the 4-7 days of heat/rut for normal Alphas and 5-14 days for Apex Alphas, plus an extra day for returning back to normal hormone levels.
Rut can be suppressed, just as heat can, though most doctors suggest not doing so. The suppressants for rut are far less tested and regulated, and there are case studies that have shown that being on suppressants for an Alpha can act like a neutering. Rut may be lost to them forever. Scent suppressants are effective, and can help the Alpha get through a sudden or unexpected rut without drawing attention to their situation.

entries.name: Nesting
entries.content:
Nesting is a common practice usually done by omegas, in which they gather up a bunch of pillows, blankets, clothes, and other soft things and lay them out in a way that forms a comfortable “nest”-like shape. Omegas often nest when they're stressed, sad, in heat, pregnant, just after giving birth, during storms etc.
Omegas start nesting at a young age, like three or four years old, not so much because they need to but because they see their mother do it and they want to do it too. They start with small nests made just about anywhere, their bed, the floor, the couch, anywhere they feel like settling. Their little nests are always filled with small blankies and stuffed toys. At this age they don't really care who is near their nest, they actually love having people around because they take pride in showing it off. As Omegas start to get older, around twelve to fourteen years old, they become very dependent on the security and comfort their nest provides. They no longer like people being around it because they're starting to be able to pick up the scents of other dynamics more and it makes them uncomfortable to have other scents on their nest besides their own. When an Omega goes into heat for the first time, around fifteen to seventeen years old, they often make a new nest in a dark and enclosed place like their closet. Absolutely no one is welcome in or near that nest, with the exception of their Omega parent who checks in with food and water every now and then, since at this age the Omega usually won't have a mate to take care of them yet. Unmated Omegas always have a nest made, mated Omegas don't though because they have an Alpha to provide them with warmth, comfort and security. Mated Omegas will usually only nest during heats, pregnancies, sicknesses and when they are extremely stressed or sad. Only their Alpha is allowed in these nests. Whenever an Omega buys a new blanket they will insist that their Alpha needs to cuddle in it with them before it can be used for a nest, because it needs to have their scents rubbed into it. Little Omega children excitedly building a big nest for them and their Alpha and Beta siblings in the living room on movie nights so they can all be cuddly and cozy together. When Omegas are building a nest they become very zoned into it and even their Alpha has difficulty getting their attention until the Omega is satisfied with it. An Alpha trying to be helpful and building a nest for their Omega who is about to go into heat, the Omega being very appreciative of the gesture but as soon as the Alpha leaves the room they rearrange everything the way they like it because Omegas are very particular about their nests. Omegas are very uncomfortable with any Alpha scent besides their mates being anywhere near their nest, the scents of other Omegas can be comforting at times though. During summer Omegas build their nests with light sheets and blankets and prefer to sleep naked because they love the soothing feel of the cool linens on their warm skin, but in winter they will use the thickest and softest blankets they can find while wearing fuzzy pajamas and snuggling as close to their Alpha as possible. They’re often compared with Omega nests and are seen as ‘unimportant’ to extremists. In stores, it’s a 50/50 for a section to be dedicated to Denning supplies.A behavior that Alpha’s hold within their inner/second Dens are the collection of comfort candles. Every inner Den has a small collection of candles with scents that you can only get from, well candles. Some Alphas light their candles and some just keep them in a box and smell the wax depending on how poor or rich the Alpha is. Alphas who have many many stuffed animals and candles dedicated to each stuffed animal!
Alpha pups / kiddies who love to observe their Alpha parent’s first den so they can make the perfect one! A first Den being set up for a high school kiddie Alpha to court an Omega or Beta or Alpha. An Alpha resting in their Omega’s nest within their first Den.

entries.name: Packs
entries.content:
Pack Leader- Pack leaders are at the top of the chain of command of their pack. Every pack has one. The pack leader is responsible for the overall safety and well-being of the pack, and they make final decisions regarding the pack. Pack leaders do not have to be alphas; they can be omegas and betas as well.
Leader’s Mate/Pack Mom- The pack leader’s mate takes the role of pack mom. The pack mom is in essence the mother figure for the entire pack. The pack may go to this individual for guidance, emotional comfort, and protection. Pack mothers are heavily involved in every day life to keep the pack running smoothly. In larger packs, pack mothers are extremely valuable.
Right Hand/s- The leader’s right hand is the member of the pack the leader trusts the most. Should something happen to the pack leader, the right hand would take over. Right hands also assist in strategic decisions for the pack. In modern days, this ranges from finances, to the pack’s pups’ education, to living situations. A pack may have more than one right hand. 
There is a subcategory of right hands called Peace Keepers. Peace keepers do exactly as their name implies: they settle arguments in the pack before it reaches the pack leader.
Left Hand/s- The pack leader’s left hand is involved in physical protection. Left hands are notoriously violent and dangerous, and they are not common in average packs. However, they may be extremely common, and even make up a majority, in packs that are involved in mafias, gangs, and the military. Basically, any pack that may be in constant danger or have threats regularly made against them will have at least one left hand.
Caretaker/s- Caretakers work under the pack mother to take care of the pack. They are usually stay-at-home pack members and do not work outside the pack. If they do work outside the pack, it is a part time job. Caretakers are involved with meals, cleaning, socialization of the pack, and managing the pups. In some packs, it is common for pack members that have recently aged out of the “pup” role to become caretakers so the pack mother can teach them how to take care of a pack, whether they stay in their current pack or leave for a different one. 
Pup/s- Pack members under the age of 17-21 (it varies from pack to pack). Pups are at the bottom of the pack hierarchy and are meant to be protected and nurtured.

entries.content: Alphas mate with omegas and claim them as their own by biting them and leaving a mating mark
